name: neural-impurity-tree-final-archive

protocol.architecture: Every completed-tree node used the same 2,497-parameter two-convolution residual binary splitter with one routing logit and no classifier head.
protocol.training: Greedy local training on hard-routed MNIST training subsets; every ancestor was frozen before descendants trained; no end-to-end gradients.
protocol.objective: Sample-weighted normalized Shannon entropy of the two differentiable children plus a label-free balance term.
protocol.expansion_policy: Use training statistics only; keep leaves at or above 90% dominant-category purity terminal.
protocol.test_policy: Construct canonical MNIST test only after the layer topology and every new splitter were fixed.

scheduled_renyi_rebuild.objective: Shannon-to-Renyi-2 schedule, temperature 2.0 to 0.25, 15% minimum-child-mass constraint, and late routing-hardness penalty.
scheduled_renyi_rebuild.first_attempt: Stopped at a depth-three node whose soft routing assigned mass to both children but whose hard threshold sent every training example to one child.
scheduled_renyi_rebuild.second_attempt: Added a sharper hard-routing-aware size surrogate, passed focused tests, and was then stopped at the user's request.

artifact_status.source_code: removed after the investigation was closed
artifact_status.checkpoints_and_generated_summaries: intentionally deleted after numerical results were archived

conclusion: The neural splitter primitive generalized, but repeated greedy expansion showed strong diminishing returns. Doubling the tree from 12 to 24 splitters improved total canonical-test impurity reduction by only 0.94 percentage points, from 34.49% to 35.43%. The investigation is complete and no classifier system was retained.
